title.text: Creator Campaign Copilot: brief to readout

n1.text:
Brief

- The brand kit prefills every field it can, so a new campaign starts mostly done.
- The live preview sits beside the form, not after it: every edit shows what followers will get, in real creators' voices.
- Check chips on the preview flag a claim or disclosure problem while it is still cheap to fix.
- Budget and the paid social CAC benchmark live here because the roster and readout both judge against them.

n2.text:
Roster

- Default sort is past CAC, cheapest first, because that is the rebooking metric.
- New creators show a 'new' tag instead of blank cells, so missing history reads as unknown, not bad.
- The budget bar updates as rows are picked; the over-budget state turns amber before it blocks.
- Mix warnings sit above the table, not in a modal: they inform the pick, they don't stop it.

n3.text:
Drafts and checks

- One row per creator, so the brand reviews a campaign the way it thinks: creator by creator.
- Failed checks block Approve and say why in plain words, with the offending phrase highlighted.
- 'Approve all passing' clears the clean rows in one click; attention goes to the flagged ones.
- Exact rules (disclosure, link, keyword, length) run in code; the model only judges paraphrased claims.

n4.text:
Creator status

- Status is a pipeline per creator: invited, accepted, connected, ready.
- Anyone not ready 3 days before their post date is flagged first, with a drafted nudge ready to send.
- A declined creator offers a backup swap right in the row, filtered to similar niche and fee.

n5.text:
Readout

- The AI brief comes first and answers the question: who to rebook, who to drop, where the budget goes.
- Every claim in the brief links to the row behind it, so the numbers can be checked.
- CAC bars draw against the paid social benchmark line: left of it beats ads, right of it loses to them.
- Reach and engagement stay in the table for context but never set the order.
